problem: The bullet mixes two different thresholds. High cavity loss or fast non-radiative decay does not stop population inversion from building up in the medium; high cavity loss only prevents the round-trip gain condition R₁R₂exp[2(g−α)L] ≥ 1 from being met, so lasing (oscillation) never starts. A student will wrongly conclude that cavity loss controls population inversion.
fix: Rewrite as: 'A bigger pump does not always give laser output. Fast non-radiative decay or a short upper-level lifetime keeps N₂ below N₁, so inversion is never reached; and even with inversion, high cavity loss or low mirror reflectance can keep the round-trip factor below 1, so oscillation never starts.'

problem: It says absorption and stimulated emission are proportional to N₁ and N₂ 'with the same Einstein B coefficient'. The two B coefficients are equal only when the degeneracies are equal; in general g₁B₁₂ = g₂B₂₁. The statement sits uneasily with the degeneracy condition given two sentences later.
fix: Say: 'The rates are B₁₂N₁ρ and B₂₁N₂ρ, where ρ is the energy density of the radiation; B₁₂ and B₂₁ are equal only when g₁ = g₂.' Then give the general condition N₂/g₂ > N₁/g₁.

problem: 'These four properties are independent' is wrong for brightness and contradicts quiz Q8: brightness depends directly on divergence (solid angle) and beam area, so poor directionality means low brightness.
fix: Say: 'The four properties are separate, but brightness is not independent of the others: a beam that is narrow in area and divergence, and carries enough power, is bright.'
